summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 2 in Infectum-wa (JTM 3.4/2)
rationale: New technical sense and Infectum-wa box; simple cotton-processing clause excludes the unrelated interviewer interruption.

Single clear cotton-processing clause with human plural agent and explicit cotton object; distinct in meaning and transitive construction from inherited lahmen. Number 2 preserves existing sense 1 pending homonym review.

summary: JTM 3.4/2 places ḥəlǧiwo u kitono after cotton picking in an Adana work narrative. The explicit cotton object and human plural subject support transitive processing; this is not an inference from the free German translation alone.

Inherited I.1 lahmen has no affected cotton object and a different meaning. Technical sense 2 is appended without renumbering; it may ultimately need a separate homonym record rather than a polysemy claim.

The plural -iwo form is filed as Infectum-wa, with no Preterit agent suffix. The narrative covers work over a two-year stay; it does not supply an additional Preterit or an independently attested new base-form pair.

No light-verb construction is present: the lexical verb directly governs u kitono. The inherited marcher lentement etymological gloss should not automatically be carried over as the etymology of cotton ginning.
Should the cotton-processing use become a separate ḥlǧ homonym with its own etymology? No new homonym key or speculative etymology is created here.
Confirm from the recording whether ḥəlǧiwo specifically denotes separating seeds from fibre, rather than another cotton-cleaning step; entkörnen is the supplied edition wording.
